items.name: Just Do It
clues: Short, tough and motivating. It makes you feel lazy for still sitting on the sofa.
Athletes, but mostly ordinary people who would like to be a bit more sporty.
An agency in Portland, Oregon, came up with it in 1988.
The very first TV ad showed an 80-year-old man running across the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.
It's one of the most famous slogans in the world, and it has been used for more than 35 years.
Three words from a sports brand with a tick-shaped logo.

items.name: Share a Coke
clues: Friendly and personal. It made people dig through the fridge at the supermarket.
Teenagers, young adults, and anyone looking for a friend's name to give as a little present.
It started in Australia in 2011.
Bottles and cans where the famous logo was replaced by people's first names.
The first version used the 150 most popular first names in the country.
A red cola can with your name on it, and an invitation to give it to someone else.

items.name: Real Beauty Sketches
clues: Quiet, emotional and a bit uncomfortable. Lots of people cried when they watched it.
Women, and anyone who has ever been too hard on themselves about how they look.
A soap and skincare brand released it in 2013, as part of a long campaign about self-esteem.
An artist sits behind a curtain and draws women only from the way they describe themselves.
The artist was trained by the FBI. Then strangers describe the same women, and the strangers' drawings are kinder.
It ends with the line “You are more beautiful than you think.” The brand's logo is a bird.

items.name: Heimkommen
clues: Very sad, then a bit happy. It isn't funny at all, but people shared it everywhere.
Families in Germany, especially grown-up children who are always too busy to visit their parents.
A German supermarket chain released it a few weeks before Christmas 2015. The Hamburg agency Jung von Matt made it.
An old man sits alone at Christmas while his children cancel their visits on the phone, one message after another.
He pretends to be dead so that the whole family finally comes home. It was the most shared German online ad of 2015.
Its title is a German hashtag that means “coming home”.

items.name: You're not you when you're hungry
aliases: You are not you when you are hungry
Youre not you when youre hungry
clues: Funny and a bit silly. It's about what happens to your personality just before lunch.
Mostly young men, but really anyone who gets grumpy when they need a snack.
It started with an ad in 2010, during the Super Bowl, America's biggest TV event of the year.
A young man playing American football in the mud is shown as a much older Hollywood actress, until he eats something.
The actress was Betty White, who was 88 at the time.
A chocolate bar with peanuts and caramel says that hunger turns you into someone else.

items.name: Priceless
clues: Warm and sentimental. It reminds you that the best moments in life aren't for sale.
Pretty much everyone with a wallet. It has been running since the 1990s.
The New York agency McCann created it in 1997.
The first ad showed a father and son at a baseball game, with a price for each little thing they paid for.
Its famous line: “There are some things money can't buy. For everything else, there's…” and then a credit card company.
One word that means “worth more than any amount of money”.
